texts.facts: The plaintiff has filed this suit against the defendant for ejectment, arrears of rent and damages. 2. In brief, the plaint averments are as under:- The defendant is the tenant under plaintiff in respect of the shop premises as described in the schedule, under lease agreement dated 20.09.2017 for a period of two years on a monthly rentals at Rs.15,000/- from 01.04.2017 subject to enhancement at 10% on every 11 months. The defendant has committed default in payment of rentals and as on 30.10.2020, he was liable to pay Rs.6,45,975/-. After adjusting the security deposit of Rs.4 lakhs, the defendant is liable to pay arrears of rent Rs.2,45,975/-. The plaintiff terminated the tenancy of the defendant by issuing a quit notice dated 10.11.2020, which was duly served upon the defendant. Thereafter, the defendant paid Rs.45,000/- which the plaintiff adjusted towards arrears of rent. Hence, prayed to direct the defendant to deliver vacant possession of the suit property and to pay arrears of rent Rs.2,15,975/- with interest at 18% per Judgment annum and damages at Rs.50,000/- per month from the date of suit till the date of handing over vacant possession of the suit property. 3. The defendant has appeared and filed written statement, which he amended subsequently, in brief is as under:- He admitted that he is a tenant under the plaintiff in respect of the suit property under the lease agreement, on security deposit of Rs.4 lakhs and monthly rentals at Rs.15,000/- per month. He has carried out repairs of the suit property and built one more floor on top at his cost by spending Rs.2,50,000/-, which the plaintiff assured to return back while delivering vacant possession of the premises. Earlier he filed a suit in OS.No.4534/2020 against the plaintiff seeking permanent injunction not to evict him from the suit property forcibly without following due process of law. The suit schedule premises measures 11.14836 sq.mtrs, which is less than 14 sq.mtrs and it is a commercial premises, so this court has no jurisdiction to try this suit. The plaintiff has received the rentals paid subsequent to issuance of notice and he is not due to pay any arrears of rent. Hence, prays to dismiss the suit. 4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the then Presiding Officer as framed issues on 20.06.2022 and additional issues on 09.06.2023 as under: Judgment M V Jaikumar vs Sendil Kumar V G on 15 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194964507/ 5. During trial, on behalf of the plaintiff, he himself got examined as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P1 to P10. On behalf of the defendant, he himself got examined as DW.1 and got marked exhibit D1 to D7. 6. The defendant issued reply notice at Ex.P7 and he sent a cheque dated 10.12.2020 for Rs.15,000/- towards rent.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the defendant, during the course of argument drew the attention of this court to Ex.P1 sale deed of the plaintiff, wherein, in the schedule, total M V Jaikumar vs Sendil Kumar V G on 15 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194964507/ 3 area mentioned is 160 sq.ft, so he said, the court has to consider only the plinth area which is 11.14836 as mentioned in Ex.P2 katha extract. 9. Per contra, the learned counsel for the plaintiff argued that 160 sq.ft amounts to 14.86448 sq.mtrs and in Ex.P2 it is clearly mentioned that there are two floors, each measuring 11.14836 sq.mtrs, so this court has jurisdiction. Of course, in Ex.P2, at the bottom, it is clearly mentioned that there are two floors, i.e. Ground and First floor, each measuring 11.14836 sq.mtrs. Further, in the plaint schedule also, the plaintiff has described the tenanted shop premises, consisting of ground floor Judgment and first floor, measuring 320 sq.ft. In fact, in para-5 of the written statement, the defendant has categorically admitted that during the pendency of the tenancy, he carried out repairs of the suit premises and built one more floor on top at his cost by spending Rs.2,50,000/-. Thereby, the defendant himself admits that there are two floors. Even in the reply notice at Ex.P7 sent by the advocate for the defendant, in reply to the quit notice issued by the advocate for the plaintiff at para-2, he mentions that the plaintiff is the owner of the shop No.85 consisting of ground and first floor. Even in the cross-examination of DW1, at page 10, when Ex.P10 photograph was confronted, he admitted that he is carrying out the business in the premises which is having both ground floor with shutter and the first floor. Thus, evidence on record could clearly show that suit schedule premises is consisting of ground and first floor and having measurement more than 22 sq.mtrs, so definitely it is more than 14 sq.mtrs, hence this court has got jurisdiction to try this suit. Of course, the learned counsel for the defendant has relied upon the decision of the Hon.ble High Court of Karnataka in K. Thimmegowda Vs. B.S. Nagaraj Rao and others, (ILR 2008 KAR 2753), wherein the Hon.ble High Court elaborately discussed what is 'plinth area' and 'carpet area' and held that in a suit for ejectment, the court has to consider the total plinth area and not carpet area. As such, the above decision, in fact, not helpful to the defendant, but clarifies the fact that the total measurement of the leased out premises in favor of the defendant consisting of more than 22 sq.mtrs plinth area. 12. However, the learned counsel for the defendant would argue, though not pleaded in the written statement or no evidence is let in that, since the plaintiff has accepted the rent, even after issuance of the quit notice, it amounts to waiver of notice, so the tenancy is not validly terminated and the defendant is entitled to continue as a tenant of the premises.
